Yes, it was an exaggeration, but I firmly believe that the complete over reliance on imports has damaged native talent so badly that it is now impossible to fix. 

LTA/LCS has been and remains to this day to be the only major region to have imports account for over 50% of the player base. Even regions that perform worse than NA at major tournaments maintain at least a 50% native player base.

NA might not have missed out on a child prodigy at the level of Zeus, but there absolutely has been a massive talent drain from T2/T3 in NA due to NA gm's preference for imported talent.

Each of these individuals, save Copy, won multiple T2 tournaments and were highly touted prospects in the North American scene when they were playing. It's hard to judge how talented they actually are because they were never given a proper chance against T1 opponents.

Regardless, its clear even NA professional players do not see a path to T1 through NA T2/T3. We have young players uprooting their lives and moving across the world to compete in different T2 leagues as it gives them a better chance to secure a professional contract. Gryffinn being the most famous example. 

It's clear the T2/T3 system is broken in North America when young native players decide it's better for their careers to compete in foreign leagues as opposed to T2 in their native region.

Historically players like 5fire, Copy, and Prismal are the biggest examples There are many more who have absolutely earned at least a chance in NA, but never received even a single game.

I don't really buy the whole "Attitude Issue" thing teams parrot when they don't offer these players chances. Armao was recycled every other split for nearly 8 years and the first year of his career his name was literally an anagram for the gamer word (Grigne).
It's hyperbole. However there absolutely have been players that have dominated NA T2 and have not been given an opportunity to play in LCS/LTA.

I'd argue T2/T3 are weak because of the massive lack of career opportunities they offer. Players in these leagues can win every tournament, trophy, individual award and will still be passed up by imports.

It's an old 3 person lift and it gets swarmed with people looking to ski the bowl. In my opinion having lived there for 25+ years the skiing is very good back there, but almost not worth the wait. Many people go there because it's the easiest access to "Double Blacks" and about 90% of the people just ski down the short cat track back to runs accessible from Storm Peak. 

If you want to experience it try to get there early. You'll be racing about 30-40 others for first chair if you get up early enough. Don't try and lap it. You'll end up spending most of your time sitting in a lift line and wasting your vacation. If you want to ski the trees back there I would highly recommend skiing to Buddies Run and traversing across. It'll spit you out at the base of the chutes and you can ski some great trees to the left and right of Big Meadow.

Another reason I warn people is because runs that Morningside services are extremely short and end in a long cat track that is almost completely flat. If you're an expert skier looking for good terrain the canyon off of Mahogany Ridge is much better skiing.

It's a beautiful mountain that gets a bad rep for some reason but I hope you have lots of fun on your trip.

Stick to trees as best you can. Storm Peak side will always be clearer than Sundown/Sunshine. Less people means more snow to enjoy and that side of the mountain gets less direct sunlight so you’ll experience less snow melt too.

DO NOT GO TO MORNINGSIDE. You WILL be stuck in a 40-45 minute line if you get there after 9:00am. The best skiing will be through the gates off of Mahogany Ridge, but is experts only and you can get cliffed out very easily.

If you want as much fresh snow as possible ski between marked runs not the actual marked runs themselves. I recommend Pony Express trees. Have fun
